raw_case_text:
A 35-year-old multiparous woman in 36th week of gestation with no significant past history presented to emergency with a short history of 8 days of malaise, chills, myalgia, jaundice, abdominal pain, and asthenia. At admission, the clinical parameters were - heart rate 120/min, blood pressure 105 / 66 mmHg, respiratory rate 17/min, axillary temperature 38 C, and oliguria of 500 ml in last 24 hours. The patient was conscious but irritable with dark icterious conjunctive and bruises in all extremities.
Earlier during her pregnancy both systolic and diastolic arterial pressures were noted to be stable. There was no history of travel abroad, contact with animals, or fever. The obstetrical examination did not reveal any genital bleeding. The laboratory parameters were: hemoglobin 10 g/dL; leukocyte count: 15,2 x 109/L including 75% neutrophils, platelets count: 40 x 109/L; C reactive protein (CRP): 115 mg/L, glucose: 0,92 g/L, creatinine: 18 mg/L and urea: 1.05 g/L, AST: 165 U/L, ALT: 145 U/L, bilirubin total: 7 mg/dl, conjugated bilirubin: 5,8 mg/dl. A moderate coagulopathy was found (PT 45%, ACT 220 seconds, D-dimer 600 ng/ml, fibrinogen 1,5 g/L), CPK: 355 U/L, troponin Ic: 0.4., Blood and urine cultures were sterile, and the serology tests for hepatitis A, B, C, cytomegalovirus, and HIV were all negative. Leptospira IgM antibodies by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay were positive at 1/300 dilution. The electrocardiogram revealed negative T waves in DII, DIII, and AVF. Ultrasound showed a single live pregnancy with oligohydramnios; Kidneys, spleen, and liver were normal and without any dilatation of the biliary canaliculi. The fetal cardiotocography was reactive. The interview of the family revealed that the patient had visited a public bath 15 days earlier. The initial management in the intensive care unit consisted of intravenous Penicillin G at 4 000 000 UI four times daily, hydration with crystalloid solutions, oxygenation by facemask. 10 hours after admission, she became severely icteric and developed severe respiratory distress with crackles on pulmonary auscultation requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. An emergency cesarean section was performed. A healthy female weighing 2.9 kg was delivered with an Apgar of 6 and 8 respectively at 1 min and 2 min after delivery. Postoperatively, X-ray chest showed bilateral diffuse opacities; blood gases showed PaO2/FiO2 < 200 and transthoracic echocardiography showed absence of increased left filling pressures fulfilling the American-European criteria for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). PAOP was not measured in the absence of Swan Ganz.
The post delivery treatment included mechanical ventilation with intravenous sedation, central venous pressure monitoring, restriction of fluid infusion and antibiotics (penicillin G). 4 days after delivery, the laboratory tests showed: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, leukocytes: 11 x 109/L, CRP: 52 mg/L, platelet: 106 x 109/L, PT: t 60%, fibrinogen: 3.5 g/l, urea: 0.55 g/L, creatinine: 11 mg/L, AST: 60 U/L, ALT: 52 U/L, troponin Ic: 0,08. Five days later, the patient's neurological and respiratory status improved, and 1 week later, she was discharged discharged from the ICU with antibiotics continued for 12 days. At follow up after 1 month of discharge the blood and urine were negative for leptospira and the neonate showed no signs of active infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 36 weeks of gestation presented with an 8-day history of malaise, chills, myalgias, jaundice, abdominal pain, and oliguria.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 8 days prior to presentation with malaise, chills, myalgias, asthenia, abdominal pain, and progressive jaundice, accompanied by oliguria (500 mL in the prior 24 hours). Ten hours after ICU admission, she deteriorated acutely with worsening jaundice and severe respiratory distress with diffuse crackles, requiring emergency endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and urgent cesarean section.
subjective.past_medical_history: Multiparous at 36 weeks of gestation with stable arterial blood pressure throughout pregnancy and no significant past medical history. Epidemiological exposure: visited a public bath 15 days prior to presentation. Denied travel abroad or direct animal contacts.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for malaise, chills, myalgias, asthenia, abdominal pain, jaundice, and dark oliguric urine. Denied vaginal/genital bleeding. Home medications and allergies are unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Heart rate: 120 beats/min; blood pressure: 105/66 mmHg; respiratory rate: 17 breaths/min; axillary temperature: 38 °C; 24-hour urine output: 500 mL. Conscious but irritable. Ocular: dark icteric conjunctivae. Skin: ecchymoses and bruises across all extremities. Obstetrical exam: no genital bleeding; reactive fetal cardiotocography. Ten hours post-admission: developed severe icterus and diffuse bilateral lung crackles with respiratory distress.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL (post-delivery: 9.8 g/dL); WBC: 15.2 x 10^9/L with 75% neutrophils (post-delivery: 11 x 10^9/L); platelets: 40 x 10^9/L (post-delivery: 106 x 10^9/L); CRP: 115 mg/L (post-delivery: 52 mg/L); glucose: 0.92 g/L; urea: 1.05 g/L (post-delivery: 0.55 g/L); creatinine: 18 mg/L (post-delivery: 11 mg/L); AST: 165 U/L (post-delivery: 60 U/L); ALT: 145 U/L (post-delivery: 52 U/L); total bilirubin: 7 mg/dL (conjugated: 5.8 mg/dL); PT: 45% (post-delivery: 60%); ACT: 220 seconds; D-dimer: 600 ng/mL; fibrinogen: 1.5 g/L (post-delivery: 3.5 g/L); CPK: 355 U/L; troponin Ic: 0.4 ng/mL (post-delivery: 0.08 ng/mL). Blood and urine cultures: sterile. Viral hepatitis A, B, and C, cytomegalovirus, and HIV serologies: negative. ECG: negative T waves in leads DII, DIII, and aVF. Ultrasound: single live intrauterine pregnancy with oligohydramnios; kidneys, spleen, and liver normal without biliary dilatation. Postoperative CXR: bilateral diffuse opacities. Blood gases: PaO2/FiO2 < 200. Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal left filling pressures.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease) presenting in the third trimester of pregnancy, complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), acute kidney injury, hepatic dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, and consumptive coagulopathy. Confirmed by positive Leptospira IgM antibodies by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) at a 1/300 dilution. Viral hepatitis (A, B, C), CMV, HIV, and bacterial sepsis were excluded. Treatment & Outcome: Managed in the ICU with intravenous penicillin G (4,000,000 UI four times daily), crystalloid hydration, emergency cesarean section delivering a healthy 2.9 kg infant (Apgar scores 6 and 8), mechanical ventilation with sedation, central venous pressure monitoring, and fluid restriction. Antimicrobial therapy was continued for 12 days. The patient experienced steady neurological and respiratory improvement, being discharged from the ICU after 1 week. Follow-up at 1 month confirmed negative Leptospira testing in blood and urine, with the infant remaining healthy and free of infection.
